response.query: What quantitative evaluation targets and per-dialect/per-category error budgets (baseline, expected gains, FPR/FNR tolerances) will define acceptance for deployment?
response.answer: For deployment, acceptable error budgets include FPR ≤ 1%, FNR ≤ 5%, and F1 Score ≥ 0.8. Baselines and gains depend on specific use cases and costs associated with false positives and negatives. Error budgets ensure reliability while allowing innovation.

results.title: What are Error Budgets? A Guide to Managing Reliability
results.content: # What are Error Budgets? Error budgets are a fundamental concept in Site Reliability Engineering that help teams balance innovation with reliability. This guide explains what error budgets are, how to manage them effectively, what to look out for, and how they differ from SLOs. Site Reliability Engineering SRE Observability SLOs Error Budgets Reliability. But what exactly are error budgets? ## What Are Error Budgets? An error budget is the acceptable amount of downtime or errors your service can experience before it violates your Service Level Objectives (SLOs). > "Error budgets give teams the freedom to innovate while maintaining accountability for reliability.". > Instead of aiming for 100% uptime (which is often unrealistic and expensive), SRE teams define acceptable failure rates and use error budgets to track them. SLOs are your target, error budgets are your tolerance for missing that target. ## How to Manage Error Budgets. Before you can have an error budget, you need SLOs. Start by identifying what matters most to your users:. Once you have SLOs, calculating the error budget is straightforward. # Error Budget Formula # ==================== # This calculates the maximum allowable downtime or failure rate # that your service can experience while still meeting your SLO. * Error Budget = 0.1% (or 8.77 hours per year). Burn rate is how quickly you're consuming your error budget. # Burn Rate Formula # ================= # This measures how fast you're consuming your error budget. A burn rate of 1 means you're consuming your error budget at the expected rate. Use your error budget to inform development decisions:. If your SLOs are too aggressive (like 99.999% uptime), your error budget becomes tiny. Using Error Budgets as Excuses. * Error Budget: 1% (adjusted for user count). Beyond the mechanics, error budgets change how teams think about reliability. Ready to implement error budgets? 3.
